title: Delete by dropping on the Trash zone, with Undo
lede: A 104×104 **Trash zone** is pinned to the bottom-right of the visible Board, above the Notes. A move hints it (`armed`); with the pointer inside it, both the zone and the Note change look (`over`); a release there deletes the Note through the same `deleteNote` as the ×, so the **Undo toast** follows. Only the pointer counts, never the Note's rect, and a resize never touches the zone. The Undo, toast and reducer actions already existed from #28.

files.question: Where is the Trash zone, and who changes its look?
files.summary: Renders the zone in the Board's viewport, outside the scroll container, inset from the scrollbars. Its `data-state` is written by the Drag engine, never by React.
files.owns: The zone's markup and its scrollbar inset.
files.never: Listens to the pointer or decides a delete.

files.question: When does a release delete instead of move?
files.summary: `moveKind` has `overTrash: pointerInTrash`, and its `commit` returns `delete` when the pointer is inside the zone. Resize kinds have no `overTrash`.
files.owns: The hit rule: the pointer itself, edges included.
files.never: Measures the DOM: the zone's rect arrives in the `DragContext`.
files.tested: Node tests in `kinds.test.ts`, including a large Note brushing the zone.

files.question: When is the zone measured, and when is each state written?
files.summary: A press measures the zone once, for a kind with `overTrash`. Each update writes `armed` or `over` only when it changes; the end writes `quiet` before resetting the Preview and dispatching.
files.owns: The edge-triggered `writeTrash` calls and their order.
files.never: Touches the DOM or knows the zone is a `div`.
files.tested: Node tests against a recording fake `DragIO`.

files.question: What does `writeTrash` do in the DOM?
files.summary: Sets `data-state` on the zone and `data-over-trash` on the dragged Note.
files.tested: Browser tests. Not in the coverage gate.

files.question: Why does a drop get Undo?
files.summary: `commit` is where a Drag saves: a `delete` goes through `deleteNote`, which ends Editing and records Undo; anything else goes straight to the Notes store.

files.question: Where does a Note's Drag save to?
files.summary: Passes `trashRef` and the `commit` command to `useDrag`, instead of `notes.dispatch`.
files.owns: Wiring a Note to the Drag engine.
files.never: Knows about the Trash zone's states.

scenarios.name: The window opens or is resized

steps.title: The scroll container changes size
steps.explain: The zone sits outside the scroll container, so it never scrolls, but the container's scrollbars come and go with the window size. The effect measures them; the CSS then puts the zone 14 px inside the visible Board's corner: the window's corner less the scrollbars and the 24 px backdrop past the Board's edge, or the Board's own corner in a window larger than the Board. So when scrolled all the way, the zone is still over the Board. Browser tests check 1024×768 scrolled to the end and a 2400×1400 window.

scenarios.name: Move a Note onto the Trash zone and release

steps.title: pointerdown on the Note
steps.explain: The zone is measured once, at press, and only for a kind that can delete. ADR 0001 pins the zone to the window, so a scroll mid-drag never moves it, and a single measurement avoids reading layout on every move. A resize gets `trash: null` and never calls `trashRect`.

run.from: const start = useDrag(ref, { scrollerRef, trashRef, commit, onClick: startEditingAt });

run.to: return rect ? { x: rect.x, y: rect.y, width: rect.width, height: rect.height } : null;

steps.title: pointermove past the Dead zone: the zone is armed
steps.explain: Every update asks the kind whether the pointer is over the zone. `setTrash` writes only on a change, so a hundred moves outside the zone write `armed` once. A Click never gets here, so it never touches the zone.

steps.title: pointermove into the zone: both change look
steps.explain: Only the pointer is tested against the zone, so a large Note whose corner covers the zone stays `armed`. `over` sets the zone red and slightly larger, and dims the Note with a dashed red outline.

steps.title: pointerup inside the zone
steps.explain: `moveKind.commit` returns `delete`. The zone goes `quiet` before the dispatch, while the Note's element still exists, so its `data-over-trash` is cleared too. The `commit` command sends the delete through `deleteNote`, which ends Editing if it was this Note and records it for Undo.

run.from: const action = commit ? s.commit(delta(s), context(s)) : null;

scenarios.name: Nothing is deleted: back out, Escape, or a resize

steps.title: pointermove back out of the zone, then pointerup
steps.explain: The state goes `over` → `armed`, then `quiet` at the end, and the commit is an ordinary `move`. The browser test drives this with real mouse input and checks both attributes after the release.

run.to: return { type: 'move', id: from.id, x, y };

steps.title: Escape over the zone
steps.explain: `end(false)` computes no action, but still writes `quiet`, so the zone and the Note never stay red after a cancel.

run.from: const action = commit ? s.commit(delta(s), context(s)) : null;

steps.title: A resize released over the zone
steps.explain: A resize kind has no `overTrash`, so `setTrash` returns at once and its `commit` never looks at the pointer. Tested in both `kinds.test.ts` and `controller.test.ts`.

notes.title: Undo restores the Note as it was at the drop, `z` included
notes.detail: The Press Raises the Note before it is dropped, so Undo brings it back on top (`z: 3` in the browser test), not at its `z` before the Drag. The counter-argument: story 41 could be read as "before I touched it". But the Raise is a real, saved action, and Undo reverses only the delete.

notes.title: The zone takes presses
notes.detail: The zone has no `pointer-events: none`. Without it, a double-click on the zone would land on the Board under it and create a Note, against story 15. The cost: a Note under the zone can't be pressed there, but it is always uncovered by scrolling (ADR 0001).

notes.title: No Board ref in `BoardDomContext`
notes.detail: The issue asked for Board, scroll container and Trash zone refs. Nothing reads a Board ref, so only `trashRef` was added.

notes.title: Hidden from assistive technology
notes.detail: The zone is `aria-hidden`: it is a pointer-only drop target. Keyboard users delete with the ×.
